```python
import dlt
from pyspark.sql.functions import col
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.getActiveSession()
catalog = spark.conf.get("catalog")
target_schema = spark.conf.get("target_schema")  # e.g., consumer_order_items_silver

# Derive bronze schema from silver target
bronze_schema = target_schema.replace("_silver", "_bronze")
bronze_table = f"{catalog}.{bronze_schema}.consumer_order_items_mv"

# Derive parent silver schema for referential integrity: replace "_items_silver" with "_order_silver"
parent_schema = target_schema.replace("_items_silver", "_order_silver")
parent_table = f"{catalog}.{parent_schema}.consumer_order_mv"

@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_order_item_id", "order_item_id IS NOT NULL")
@dlt.expect_or_drop("valid_fk_order_items_to_order", "parent_order_id IS NOT NULL")
@dlt.table(
    name="consumer_order_items_mv",
    comment="Silver order item view with validated data",
    table_properties={"quality": "silver"},
    schema="""
        order_item_id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
        order_id INT NOT NULL,
        product_id INT NOT NULL,
        quantity INT NOT NULL,
        unit_price DOUBLE NOT NULL,
        total_price DOUBLE NOT NULL,
        parent_order_id INT
    """
)
def consumer_order_items_mv():
    # Read from bronze table as a batch source
    df = spark.read.table(bronze_table)
    # Referential integrity check: validate order_id references consumer_order.consumer_order_mv
    parent_df = spark.read.table(parent_table).select(col("order_id").alias("parent_order_id"))
    df = df.join(parent_df, df["order_id"] == parent_df["parent_order_id"], "left")
    return df
```
